# Function Overriding

#### Course: Learn C++ OOP

## Function Overriding

```cpp
1#include <iostream>
2using namespace std;
3
4class Animal {
5    public:
6
7
8        // make_sound() function of base class
9        void make_sound() {
10            cout << "Animal Sound" << endl;
11        }
12
13};
14
15class Dog: public Animal {
16    public:
17
18
19        // make_sound() function of derived class
20        void make_sound() {
21            cout << "Woof Woof" << endl;
22        }
23
24};
25
26int main() {
27
28    // create object of child class Dog
29    Dog dog1;
30
31
32    // access function of Dog class  
33    dog1.make_sound();
34
35
36    return 0;
37}
38
39// Output: Woof Woof
```

Here, the make_sound() function is present in both the Dog class and the Animal class. However, when we call the function using the dog1 object, the function of the Dog class is executed.

This is because the function in the child class (Dog) overrides the same function in the parent class (Animal). And this process is known as function overriding.
